narrative: OMX30 enters Friday supported by broad Asia-US rally (correlation signal +0.571%), though technical setup warns of caution. The index sits +6.8% above its 200-MA in full bull regime, but ADX at 2.7 signals weak trend conviction with bearish directional bias—a red flag requiring confidence reduction per risk rules. Copper strength (+1.12%) is a tailwind for Boliden and cyclicals, while USD/SEK depreciation (9.557, -0.76%) supports Volvo, Atlas Copco, and Ericsson exporters despite NASDAQ's +1.4% lift. MACD remains below signal and RSI sits at neutral 52.75, leaving room for mean-reversion upside if technicals align, but weak ADX means magnitude should be tempered. Key watch: US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET and any inflation surprises that could reverse the 71bp yield decline.
morningBrief: OMX30 set for modest +0.4% open on tailwinds from Asia (Hang Seng +1.74%) and US tech (NASDAQ +1.40%), but watch the weak ADX (2.7) — conviction is low and directional bias is bearish. Support at 3085 (lower Bollinger), resistance at 3180 (50-MA); pivot 3123. Banks get a modest positive from yield compression; Boliden stands out on copper rally (+1.12%) and gold strength (+0.54%). Exporters (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson) benefit from USD/SEK weakness, but NASDAQ's jump is partly offset by sentiment risk in Ericsson/Hexagon if tech momentum fades. VIX 14.24 is calm, but US Jobless Claims (14:30 CET) is the day's economic flashpoint—miss could reignite rate volatility. Trade tight ranges until data; avoid overstaying bull positions given weak trend structure.
